question: What is the primary format of a partograph?
explanation: The partograph uses a pictorial and graphic layout to display labour data clearly on a single sheet. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h1)

question: Why is the partograph considered an early warning system?

options.A: It predicts the exact hour of spontaneous delivery
options.B: It highlights deviations from normal labour progress early
options.C: It detects genetic abnormalities in the unborn baby
options.D: It measures the mother's baseline blood pressure accurately

explanation: Visual tracking helps nurses spot delayed progress or distress before severe complications happen. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h1)

question: An obstructed labour is best prevented by which benefit of the partograph?

options.C: Lowering the cost of hospital admission

explanation: Spotting delayed cervical dilation early stops labour from progressing into dangerous obstruction. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h2)

question: How does the partograph improve shift handovers among nurses?

options.A: By eliminating the need for verbal reports
options.B: By predicting the exact shift delivery numbers
options.C: By presenting standardized, clear visual data
options.D: By replacing the patient's bedside admission folder

explanation: A graphical layout allows incoming staff to assess the entire history of the labour at a quick glance. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h2)

question: How often should cervical dilation be plotted on the active phase partograph?
explanation: Standard protocol requires cervical assessment and plotting every four hours during active labour. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h3)

question: Which parameter under maternal condition is monitored most frequently?
explanation: Maternal pulse is usually checked every thirty minutes to one hour, whereas blood pressure is checked every four hours. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h3)

question: What does a meconium-stained amniotic fluid recording usually indicate on the partograph?

options.D: Normal progression of the first stage

explanation: Passing meconium in utero typically signals that the foetus has experienced oxygen deprivation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h4)

question: When is the best time to count the foetal heart rate during labour?

options.A: During the peak of a strong contraction
options.C: Only when the mother feels active kicks

explanation: Counting right after a contraction helps assess how the foetus recovers from the temporary drop in blood flow during the contraction. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h4)

question: What is the expected minimum rate of cervical dilation during active labour?
explanation: Normal active labour progresses at a minimum speed of 1 cm of cervical dilation every hour. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h5)

question: How are uterine contractions represented on the progress of labour grid?

options.C: By shading grid squares based on duration

explanation: Contraction length is visualized by shading boxes corresponding to how many seconds each contraction lasts. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h5)

question: How frequently should maternal blood pressure be recorded on a standard partograph?
explanation: Standard guidelines specify checking maternal blood pressure every four hours unless complications require tighter monitoring. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h6)

question: A rising maternal temperature logged every 4 hours on the partograph most likely points to what condition?
explanation: Elevated temperature during prolonged labour often signals intrauterine infection, requiring prompt medical review. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h6)

question: At what cervical dilation does the alert line on the partograph begin?
explanation: The alert line marks the official onset of the active phase of labour, starting at 4 cm dilation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h7)

question: What action is required when the cervical dilation curve crosses the action line?

options.A: Discharging the patient home for rest
options.C: Waiting another four hours to observe progress
options.D: Immediate medical evaluation and definitive intervention

explanation: Crossing the action line means labour is severely delayed, requiring prompt clinical action like a Caesarean section or oxytocin. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h7)

question: When should entries be made on the partograph during labour?

options.A: When the doctor arrives for ward round
options.C: In real time as observations are made
options.D: From memory at the end of the shift

explanation: Immediate documentation prevents errors and ensures an accurate timeline of the labour process. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h8)

question: What is the primary responsibility of a nurse when a partograph shows abnormal trends?

options.A: Wait for the patient to request pain medication
options.B: Convert the partograph into a narrative case study
options.C: Hide the chart to prevent panic in the labour ward
options.D: Interpret the trends and initiate timely referrals or actions

explanation: Nurses must use the tool actively to catch delays early and trigger prompt multidisciplinary care. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h8)
